concepts.def: The eleven years Charles I governed without Parliament, raising revenue by controversial means like Ship Money, deepening conflict with his subjects.
Parliament summoned by Charles I to fund war with Scotland, which instead attacked royal policies, escalating tensions toward civil war.
Armed conflict between Royalists supporting the king and Parliamentarians, ending in defeat for Charles I and the rise of the New Model Army.
The trial and beheading of Charles I for treason against his people, an unprecedented act establishing a republican Commonwealth.
The return of the monarchy under Charles II after the collapse of the republic, restoring king, Lords and the Church of England.
The overthrow of James II and accession of William and Mary, leading to the Bill of Rights and a constitutional limit on royal power.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Britain 1625-1701: Conflict, Revolution & Settlement — a core area of A-Level History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Britain 1625-1701: Conflict, Revolution & Settlement brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Britain 1625-1701: Conflict, Revolution & Settlement.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the period 1629-40 when Charles I ruled without Parliament called?
options: The Personal Rule
The Restoration
The Interregnum
The Protectorate

mcqs.q: What happened to Charles I in 1649?
options: He was tried and executed
He fled to France
He abdicated peacefully
He defeated Parliament

mcqs.q: What did the Restoration of 1660 bring back?
options: The monarchy under Charles II
A republic
Catholic rule of England
Oliver Cromwell

mcqs.q: What was the outcome of the Glorious Revolution of 1688?
options: William and Mary replaced James II
Charles I returned to the throne
England became a republic
The Pope ruled England

mcqs.q: Why did the English Civil War break out in 1642?
options: The Civil War was simply about whether England should be Catholic or Protestant.
It arose from disputes over royal power, religion and money between Charles I and Parliament, not from a single cause.
It restored Catholic monarchy to England.
The Civil War was a foreign invasion of England.

mcqs.q: Did the execution of Charles I create lasting republican government?
options: It produced the Commonwealth and Cromwell's Protectorate, but the monarchy was restored in 1660, showing the republic was unstable.
Charles I's son was also executed in 1649.
The Civil War was a foreign invasion of England.
England remained a permanent republic after 1649.

mcqs.q: What did the Glorious Revolution of 1688 settle?
options: It established that monarchs ruled with Parliament's consent, confirmed by the Bill of Rights, limiting royal power permanently.
The Glorious Revolution made England a republic.
The Civil War was a foreign invasion of England.
It restored Catholic monarchy to England.
